html:
Babi Yar is a ravine in Kyiv where German forces shot 33,771 Jews over two days, 29 and 30 September 1941, ten days after taking the city, one of the largest single massacres of the Holocaust.

Notices ordered the Jews of Kyiv to gather with their papers and belongings. They were marched to the ravine, made to undress and shot in groups by an SS unit with the help of German police and local auxiliaries. Over the next two years tens of thousands more, including Roma, Soviet prisoners and Ukrainian nationalists, were killed there. Soviet authorities long refused to name the Jewish victims. Yevgeny Yevtushenko's poem Babi Yar of 1961 and Shostakovich's 13th Symphony broke the silence. A memorial complex is being built there; a Russian missile struck nearby in 2022 during the invasion of Ukraine.
sum: Babi Yar is a ravine in Kyiv where German forces shot 33,771 Jews over two days, 29 and 30 September 1941, ten days after taking the city, one of the largest single massacres of the Holocaust.
